primary.title: 仕事を読み解くキーワード：遊んでくださる人のことを第一に
primary.speaker: Ueda, graphics programmer; official page identifies work on Splatoon and Splatoon 2
primary.historicalScope: Splatoon 2 (2017) development; not an assertion of Splatoon 3 shader internals
primary.readScope: Entire article, all instructional paragraphs, captions and employee bio; all three linked full comparison images viewed.
facts: Splatoon 1 ink was reported excessively shiny in some stages or too flat-looking.
Splatoon 2 development adopted physically based shading to improve ink appearance.
Dark shading on raised ink made team-color boundaries harder to distinguish.
Removing shading made floor/wall geometry harder to distinguish.
Raising specular-reflection intensity made splashes when an enemy transformed and submerged harder to see.
The team discussed priorities across sections and prioritized playability; adjustment continued into the demo period.
notDisclosed: Exact shipped shader formulas, BRDF coefficients, shadow-remapping curves or numerical thresholds.
The ink-paint attachment, UV, render-texture, collision or networking implementation.

imageReadNotes.caption: チーム色の違いをならす
imageReadNotes.observation: Six paired team-color views; brighter/flat top and more shaded bottom appearances. Caption concerns leveling team-color differences; do not assign an undocumented exact shader setting to any tile.

imageReadNotes.caption: どんなライティング環境でも映えるように
imageReadNotes.observation: Same indoor ramp, wall and two ink colors in paired views, with visibly different brightness. It demonstrates a development comparison, not our independent recording.

imageReadNotes.caption: 何もしていないモノと最終結果の比較
imageReadNotes.observation: Paired wall/floor views; the final-looking right image preserves stronger magenta/green visibility in shaded parts. Caption explicitly compares untreated and final results, but gives no formula.
